## Claims
- [source-backed] The paper formally conjectures that both Theorem 5.4 generating sets for \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) are minimal. [source-6, lines 14-16]
- [proved] Conditional on the integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation, in the boundary subcase
  \[
  p=q-i=1,\qquad c=r-j\ge2,\qquad \min(i,j)=2,
  \]
  the degree-\(\le d+2\) quotient of \(Q=J/A_+J\), \(d=ij\), is
  \[
  Q_d\oplus Q_{d+1}\oplus Q_{d+2}
  \cong \mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2.
  \]
  Moreover \(\bar y_1=-\bar x_1\) and \(\bar y_2=\bar x_2\).
- [proved] This low-degree certificate alone does not imply \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^3\): a graded abelian group may agree through degree \(d+2\) and have an additional nonzero summand in degree \(d+3\).

## Strategy
Let
\[
x_0=s_{i^j},\quad x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\quad
y_1=s_{(i^j,1)},
\]
\[
x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})},\quad
z=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1},1)},\quad
y_2=s_{(i^j,2)},\quad w=s_{(i^j,1,1)}.
\]
For \(p=1,c\ge2\), \(u=s_{(i+2,i^{j-1})}\) is outside the box, whereas \(w\) remains inside. The complete Pieri rows are
\[
h_1x_0=x_1+y_1,
\]
and, on columns \((x_2,z,y_2,w)\),
\[
h_2x_0=z+y_2,\qquad
h_1x_1=x_2+z,\qquad
h_1y_1=z+y_2+w.
\]
Thus the degree-\(d+2\) matrix is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
0&1&1&0\\
1&1&0&0\\
0&1&1&1
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its restriction to complementary columns \((z,y_2,w)\) has determinant
\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\1&0&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}=-1.
\]
Hence these rows integrally eliminate \((z,y_2,w)\), leaving \(\bar x_2\) freely. The degree-\(d+1\) row similarly leaves \(\bar x_1\) freely, with \(\bar y_1=-\bar x_1\), and the first two degree-\(d+2\) rows give \(\bar y_2=\bar x_2\).

## Gaps
- This is conditional on the stated box, Schur-span, and integral Pieri hypotheses.
- It treats only \(p=1,c\ge2\) and only degrees through \(d+2\).
- Independent review is still required.
- No generation or minimality conclusion follows.

## Next
- Separate follow-on: treat the opposite boundary
  \[
  c=r-j=1,\qquad p=q-i\ge2,\qquad \min(i,j)=2.
  \]
- Separate follow-on: prove a graded-kernel/global elimination statement in every degree, including saturation, before asserting any global structure of \(J/A_+J\) or any parent theorem.
